results.response:
"The Arab Tent" is an oil‑on‑canvas painted around 1865‑66 by the English artist Edwin (Henry) Landseer, best known for his animal subjects. The work was exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1866 under the title “Mare and Foal – Indian Tent…,” though the tent depicted is clearly Arab.

In the bustling scene you’ll see an Arab mare with her foal, two Persian greyhounds, and two mischievous monkeys—one wearing an earring. A jar with two pipes on the right hints at the owner’s presence. It’s a rare example of Landseer tackling the fashionable Orientalist theme of his day.

The painting was bought by the Prince of Wales in 1867 and then acquired by Sir Richard Wallace in 1878 for £6,300, making it one of the most expensive pieces ever bought for the Wallace Collection. Today it hangs in the Hall, and its recent conservation in 2017 was made possible by the generous support of Henrietta, Duchess of Bedford.
